payload.proof_nl:
Let X and Y be finite sets, and assume there exists an injective function f : X -> Y. We must prove that |X| <= |Y|.

Because Y is finite, every subset of Y is finite, and its cardinality is at most |Y|. Consider the image f(X) = {f(x) : x in X}. Since f(X) is a subset of Y, it follows that f(X) is finite and
|f(X)| <= |Y|.

Now we use injectivity of f to compare X and f(X). The map f, viewed as a function from X onto f(X), is surjective by definition of image. It is also injective by hypothesis. Hence f : X -> f(X) is a bijection. Therefore X and f(X) have the same cardinality:
|X| = |f(X)|.

Combining the two facts,
|X| = |f(X)| <= |Y|,
so |X| <= |Y|, as required.

payload.statement_nl: Let X and Y be finite sets. If there exists an injective function f : X -> Y, then the cardinalities satisfy |X| <= |Y|.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly uses the image subset f(X) ⊆ Y and finiteness of Y to infer |f(X)| ≤ |Y|.
The proof correctly observes that f viewed as X → f(X) is surjective by definition of image and injective by hypothesis, hence bijective.
The conclusion |X| = |f(X)| ≤ |Y| is valid and establishes the desired inequality with no missing cases.

result_payload.reason: The proof is mathematically correct and complete for finite sets: it forms the image f(X) ⊆ Y, uses injectivity to show f : X → f(X) is a bijection, concludes |X| = |f(X)|, and combines this with |f(X)| ≤ |Y|. This matches the lemma statement exactly and supports the root theorem role of turning an injection into a cardinality inequality.
